messages.subject: Conditional Action Button?
parts:
So, I am a very avid user of Shiny but I am currently having a mental stump (maybe because its friday @.@) which I am hoping someone might be able to assist with. The issue is that I have several panels that all rely on each other. The goal is to output the plot(s). In certain cases, I want the plot to specifically not auto generate. Instead, I want the plot to be reliant on an action button. 

##  startSubset and startGroup are button parameters
observeEvent(c(input$startSubset, input$startGroup), {
                     values$wait<- F
             })
observe({
    output$plot <-  renderPlot({
          p <- preliminaryFunction(file, input, values)
          if (!is.null(p)) {
            if(input$group || input$subset ){
              if(!values$wait){
                print(p)
                values$wait<-T
              }
            }
            else{
              print(p)
            }
         }
      })
})

This is just a snippet of my current code. Unfortunately, because I have values$wait<- T and shiny is running the observer 2 times for this change, I am not generating the graph that I want. I am unable to stop the multiple renderings for this function because it is needed due to required parameters being changed. This is just one of the many solutions I have tried. I have attempted breaking the plot rendering into 2 functions where one would not generate if the parameters for the other were valid, I have tried to isolate different parts of my code etc. I feel like this should be fairly simple and I just keep missing it by a hair. 


So, my question is this: how can I make my code conditionally dependent on an action button when very specific parameters are used ? 

Thanks in advance!

Amber James

messages.subject: Re: Conditional Action Button?
parts:
It's ok. I figured out my problem. It seems that my brain was indeed turned off because it was Friday. >.< 

I needed to assign my input variable to a reactive variable and only reassign the reactive variable when the button was clicked.
##  startSubset and startGroup are button parameters

observeEvent(c(input$startSubset), {
                    values$subsetRowSelected<- input$subset_rows_selected
            })
observeEvent(c(input$startGroup), {
                   values$groupRowSelected <-  input$group_rows_selected
           })

I was previously using the input rows selected all over the place. This was causing me issues because shiny would recall my functions over and over. With this I can specifically control the reallocation of the row selected values. It also means that my plot wont regenerate unless the button is clicked.  :D 

Thank you for you help Dean Attali. I appreciate the reach out! 

Amber James
